current_example.problem:
Find an integral expression that gives the shaded area between the polar curves $r=2\cos(3\theta)$ and $r=1,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226762/assets/9fdeb4d842f141d702027e7a2ec3e7618eacd57c3c97119f851dd2497d8ee813.png)
current_example.worked_solution:
Consider the rightmost petal, oriented along the $x$-axis. First, we find the values of $\theta$ for which the two curves intersect:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta ) & =1 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta ) & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two solutions for $3\theta \in \left[-\pi,\pi\right]\mathbin{:}$

$$
3\theta = -\dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{\pi}{3} \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad \theta= -\dfrac{\pi}{9}, \dfrac{\pi}{9}
$$

To determine the inner function and the outer, let's draw an arrow from the origin that passes through the shaded region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14226762/assets/8950c8f5e8ea54736714e83f584ccc4b164cdee53cf3c3f64a8e0c9f81f16e6a.png)

The arrow

- *enters* the region through the inner function $r=1,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer function $r=2\cos(3\theta).$

To find the area, we use the formula

$$
A = \dfrac{1}{2} \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} \Big( \big[ {\color{brown}\text{outer}} \big]^2 - \big[ {\color{blue}\text{inner}} \big]^2 \Big) \:\textrm{d}\theta,
$$

where

$\qquad$ $\theta_1=-\dfrac{\pi}{9}, \quad$ and $\quad \theta_2=\dfrac{\pi}{9}.$ 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /9}^{\pi /9}[{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta ))}^{2}-{1}^{2}]\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-\pi /9}^{\pi /9}(4{cos}^{2}⁡(3\theta )-1)\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$
